clue.text: Bird conspicuous on Ilkley Moor?

definitions.meaning: a castrated cockerel fattened for the table
the Yorkshire song 'On Ilkla Moor Baht 'at' is about going there hatless, so headwear worn there would stand out

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher asks which species stands out on a bleak Yorkshire moor.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as CAP ON: the song 'On Ilkla Moor Baht 'at' (without a hat) makes a hat on your head the odd thing out there. Ilkley Moor is in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A gelded cockerel raised for meat is a poultry bird.

clue.text: Instrument groom takes to hide in box?

definitions.text: Instrument groom takes to hide in box?

parts.words: Instrument groom takes to hide in box?
parts.note: a stable groom uses a toothed tool on a horse's hide in its loose box; 'curry' also means to dress leather, punning on hide

explanation.surface: A bridegroom seems to grab some implement and duck into a cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The groom is a stable hand, the hide is a horse's coat, and the box is a horsebox or loose box, not a wedding-day hiding place.
explanation.definitionFit: This toothed tool is what grooms rub over a horse's coat to loosen dirt and hair.

clue.text: Person on TV taken from those eligible for jury-service

definitions.meaning: a member of a quiz or discussion team on a television show

definitions.text: taken from those eligible for jury-service
definitions.meaning: drawn from the ..., the roll of people who may be called as jurors

explanation.surface: A television personality is picked from the pool of possible jurors.
explanation.definitionFit: A guest who sits on a broadcast quiz team is a panel member; split, the word is also a jury roll.

clue.text: Lone ranger a coward, we hear?

indicators.note: a ranger roams about, so these letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone says the solitary cowboy hero is really a yellow-bellied coward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lone ranger' summons the masked Western hero, but 'ranger' is the anagram signal on LONE. The definition points to the playwright Noel Coward: 'a Coward' by first name.
explanation.definitionFit: The English playwright and wit Coward had this first name.

clue.text: Frustrate everybody at Arden, for example

parts.note: the Forest of Arden is the woodland setting of Shakespeare's As You Like It
everybody means all

explanation.surface: Every member of the cast at the Arden woodland scene thwarts the plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Arden is the Forest of Arden, the woodland of Shakespeare's As You Like It.
explanation.definitionFit: To head someone off by acting first is to thwart or prevent them.

clue.text: Bureau of overseas post

parts.note: overseas means foreign
a post is a job or position, an office

explanation.surface: An office that handles mail sent abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Post' reads as mail, but here it is a job: an office. The British government department for overseas affairs was long called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's department of state for external affairs is a government bureau.

clue.text: Stern half of flood-vessel found in Channel Islands

indicators.note: only the rear half of the vessel's name survives, the front half dropped

parts.note: the vessel of the Biblical Flood is Noah's Ark

explanation.surface: The back half of a boat carried by floodwater washes up in the Channel Islands.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first half, NOAH, from NOAHSARK (Noah's Ark) and keep the stern half.
explanation.definitionFit: This small island lies among the Channel Islands between England and France.

clue.text: Lear, I turn out to appear in The Tempest

indicators.note: to turn out is to come out differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor known for King Lear says he will take a part in another Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn out' rearranges LEAR and I. Both plays are Shakespeare's, which hides the switch from character to anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: The airy spirit serving Prospero is a character in this Shakespeare play.

clue.text: The French can appear rather volatile in temperament

parts.note: la is a French word for the
a can is a tin

explanation.surface: French people can seem rather hot-headed by nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The French' is the French article LA, not a nation's character.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiery, passionate disposition is stereotypically called this, after southern European peoples.

clue.text: Run from a sweep

definitions.meaning: to extend between limits, as prices that go from one figure to another
an extent or span, as of hills or of vision

explanation.surface: Flee from a chimney cleaner.
explanation.definitionFit: Prices that stretch across limits do this; an expanse or scope is also so called.

clue.text: Coach in refreshment stop

indicators.note: in places the one word within the other

parts.note: a rest is refreshment for the weary
to coach is to train

explanation.surface: A motor coach pulls into a service station for refreshments.
explanation.walkthrough: Coach is a verb, train, not a bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding back or checking something is a curb on it, a stop.

clue.text: Safety-catch in estate-car?

definitions.meaning: read literally, a brake on a shooting gun
an old name for a station wagon

explanation.surface: A gun's safety lock found inside a family car.
explanation.definitionFit: A dated British name for a station wagon; taken literally it is a brake for firing.

clue.text: The old record for a quick cry

parts.note: ye is the archaic form of the
LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A vintage vinyl album sells for a brief shout.
explanation.definitionFit: A short sharp shriek, as of a dog in pain, is a quick cry.

clue.text: Focal point of big mug about four

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: a pot can be a large drinking vessel
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Four people gather round a huge mug of tea at the heart of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A central pin or point on which things turn is a focal point.

clue.text: Open tart left in cooler

indicators.note: in places one letter inside the word for a cooler

parts.note: a fan cools you

explanation.surface: An uncovered pastry was left in the fridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' suggests a fridge, but it is a FAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry case with a filling and no lid is an open tart.

clue.text: Tender of dyke-builder is heard

indicators.note: is heard says the king's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Offa, an 8th-century Mercian king, built Offa's Dyke along the Welsh border

explanation.surface: A bid from the man who built an earthwork is reported.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa's Dyke is a great earthwork along the England-Wales border, named after King Offa of Mercia.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender is a formal bid or proposal.

clue.text: Like botanical gardens on one side?

parts.note: like means as
Kew Gardens in London is the Royal Botanic Gardens

explanation.surface: A question whether a famous garden lies lopsided.
explanation.walkthrough: Kew Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in south-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something at a slant or crooked is set to one side.

clue.text: Negligible inane film, is it, being developed?

indicators.note: developing a film changes it, so these letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone wonders if a silly movie still in the darkroom amounts to anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being developed' rearranges INANE FILM IS IT; 'film' and 'developed' make a photographic picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Something so tiny it is next to nothing is negligible.

clue.text: Give wrong route, having cried out in fog

indicators.note: in places the scrambled word inside the word for fog

parts.note: mist is a light fog

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the word is jumbled

explanation.surface: A lost traveller shouts in the fog after being sent the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' turns CRIED into DIREC, and 'in' puts that inside MIST.
explanation.definitionFit: To send someone the wrong way is to point them on a mistaken route.

clue.text: Final desperate effort in closing dump

parts.note: closing means last
to dump something is to ditch it

explanation.surface: A last-gasp try made while a rubbish tip is shutting.
explanation.definitionFit: A final stand, from defending the furthest trench, is a desperate last attempt.

clue.text: Fat digits make a poor fielder

parts.note: butter is a fat
fingers are digits

explanation.surface: Greasy hands make a cricketer drop catches.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the fielders try to catch the ball; one who drops it is mocked with this name.
explanation.definitionFit: A clumsy person who drops catches is a poor fielder.

clue.text: Mark in police-station, or…

definitions.meaning: British slang for a police station

explanation.surface: A scratch inside a police station, or else...
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into the next clue, which uses this word's sense of prison.
explanation.definitionFit: A small notch is a mark; British slang also uses the word for a station house of police.

clue.text: Plane-crash in mountainous country

indicators.note: a crash wrecks things, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An aircraft comes down in the Himalayas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan kingdom is a mountainous country.

clue.text: Lance treated to be sterile

indicators.note: treated means worked on, so the letters are processed into a new order

explanation.surface: A boil is lanced and treated to keep it germ-free.
explanation.definitionFit: Free of germs or dirt is sterile.

clue.text: … prison, with ring on leg?

parts.note: a leg is a limb
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Continuing the last clue, a jail where a ring is fixed to a prisoner's leg.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang for jail; it also means a state of confinement.

clue.text: Watch marbles?

definitions.meaning: to look after or take care with
slang for one's wits, as in 'lose your marbles'

explanation.surface: Keep an eye on the glass balls.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking care of something is to look after it; one's wits are one's marbles.

clue.text: Many going to hospital are so reluctant

parts.note: a lot means many

explanation.surface: Crowds heading into hospital are unwilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwilling or disinclined is reluctant.

clue.text: Station-halt

definitions.meaning: a place where trains or buses pull up

explanation.surface: A minor railway halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopping place on a route is a station; to cease is to halt.

clue.text: Spectacles of women only, presumably, in untidy heap

indicators.note: in places the phrase meaning no men within the jumbled word
untidy means messed up, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
a women-only gathering has no men

explanation.surface: Glasses belonging to women are found in a messy pile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'untidy' jumbles HEAP to PHEA, and 'in' puts NO MEN inside it. 'Spectacles' means sights, not glasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable sights or events are spectacles.

clue.text: Lifting the foot that is shortened

parts.note: the word foot is abbreviated to FT

explanation.surface: Picking up a foot, which is then cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifting is slang for stealing.

clue.text: Pine cabin for the people of Borneo?

definitions.text: Pine cabin for the people of Borneo?

parts.words: Pine cabin for the people of Borneo?
parts.note: pine also means yearn or long, and the cabin is the communal dwelling of Borneo's peoples

explanation.surface: A wooden hut built for Borneo tribespeople.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like the wood but is the verb, to long; Borneo's Dayak peoples traditionally live in long communal dwellings.
explanation.definitionFit: A long communal timber dwelling is home to Borneo's Dayak peoples.

clue.text: Launch to flounder

definitions.meaning: to lurch or plunge forward, as a ship in heavy seas

explanation.surface: A boat set afloat starts struggling.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurl something is to launch it; a ship plunging in waves founders and lurches.
